Nicknamed "'''Stix'''", he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]]. Smith was picked 10th overall in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]]. During his rookie season with the Suns, he reached the [[NBA Finals]]. In February 2022, he was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]]. ==Early life== Smith was born in [[Portsmouth, Virginia]] to Charles and Orletha Smith.{{cite web |title=USA Basketball Bio |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/s/smith-jalen.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160611100217/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/s/smith-jalen.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 11, 2016 |website=usab.com |publisher=USA Basketball |access-date=August 25, 2018}} Smith attended [[Mount Saint Joseph High School]] in [[Baltimore]], [[Maryland]] where he averaged 22.2 points, 12.0 rebounds, and 4.0 blocks per game as a senior and won several awards, among them, the Gatorade Maryland Boys Basketball Player of the Year twice.{{cite web |last1=Cann |first1=Harrison |title=Jalen Smith made Terps fans excited about the future at the McDonald's All-American Game |url=http://www.dbknews.com/2018/03/30/jalen-smith-basketball-recruiting-mcdonalds-all-american-game/ |publisher=[[The Diamondback]] |access-date=August 25, 2018 |date=March 30, 2018}} He was named to the [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018 McDonald's All-American]] team.{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Top players named to McDonald's All-American teams |url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/22122836 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |access-date=August 25, 2018 |date=March 23, 2023}} Smith was ranked among the top 25 prospects of the 2018 recruiting class by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[247Sports]], and [[ESPN]]. Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] in 2020]] On November 8, 2017, Smith signed his [[National Letter of Intent]] to play for [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] after verbally committing in June.{{cite web |last1=Ermann |first1=Jeff |title="Sticks" is on Board with Maryland |url=https://247sports.com/college/maryland/Article/Jalen-Smith-Signs-with-Terps-Maryland-Basketball-Adds-Recruit-on-Signing-Day-110162866/ |website=247sports.com |publisher=247Sports |access-date=August 25, 2018 |date=November 8, 2017}} He selected Maryland over programs such as [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].{{cite web |last1=Geary |first1=Molly |title=Jalen Smith Is a Crucial Piece for Maryland as the Terps Aim for a Bounce-Back Year |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/08/21/maryland-terrapins-recruiting-jalen-smith |website=SI.com |publisher=Sports Illustrated |access-date=August 25, 2018 |date=August 21, 2018}} As a freshman, he averaged 11.7 points, 6.8 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game. He had 19 points and 12 rebounds in a 79–77 win over [[Belmont Bruins men's basketball|Belmont]] in the Round of 64 of the NCAA Tournament. In the next game, a 69–67 loss to [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], Smith finished with 15 points, eight rebounds and a career-high five blocks.{{cite news |last1=Markus |first1=Don |title=Jalen Smith will return for sophomore year at Maryland for a multitude of reasons — including his education season, Smith declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=Maryland's Jalen Smith declares for NBA draft |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/04/07/jalen-smith/ |access-date=April 7, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=April 7, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Phoenix Suns (2020–2022)=== Smith was selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the 10th pick in the first round of the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Oyefusi |first1=Daniel |title=Maryland's Jalen Smith selected No. 10 overall by Phoenix Suns in NBA draft |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2020/11/18/marylands-jalen-smith-picked-no-10-overall-by-phoenix-suns-in-nba-draft-i-just-cant-wait-to-get-started/ |access-date=November 18, 2020 |work=[[Baltimore Sun]] |date=November 18, 2020}} On November 24, 2020, the [[Phoenix Suns]] announced that they had signed Smith.{{cite web|title=Suns sign Jalen Smith & Ty-Shon Alexander|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/draft/suns-sign-jalen-smith-ty-shon-alexander|date=November 24, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 24, 2020}} On February 15, 2021, due to the team's success and after appearing in only eight games, the Suns assigned Smith to the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web | last=Anderson | first=Jake | title=Phoenix Suns assign rookie Jalen Smith to NBA G League | website=Arizona Sports | date=2021-02-15 | url=https://arizonasports.com/nba/phoenix-suns/phoenix-suns-assign-rookie-jalen-smith-to-nba-g-league/2545094/ | access-date=2025-12-07}} On February 26, 2021, the Suns recalled Smith.{{Cite web|date=2021-02-26|title=Jalen Smith recalled from G League by Phoenix Suns|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2558468/jalen-smith-recalled-from-g-league-by-phoenix-suns/|access-date=2021-03-10|website=Arizona Sports}} Smith ended his rookie season by making the [[2021 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], but the Suns were defeated in six games by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], as well as future Pacers teammate [[Jordan Nwora]]. ===Indiana Pacers (2022–2024)=== On February 10, 2022, Smith was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] along with a future second-round draft pick ([[Hugo Besson]]) in exchange for [[Torrey Craig]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-acquire-jalen-smith-and-2022-second-round-pick-suns|title=Pacers Acquire Jalen Smith and 2022 Second-Round Pick from Suns|work=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2022}} On July 1, 2022, Smith re-signed with the Pacers on a two-year deal worth $9.6 million. After the signing, Pacers head coach [[Rick Carlisle]] announced Smith would be a starter and considered him an "important part of our future."{{cite web|url=https://hoopshype.com/2022/11/03/rick-carlisle-calls-jalen-smith-an-important-part-of-our-future/|title=Rick Carlisle calls Jalen Smith an 'important part of our future'|work=HoopsHype.com|date=November 3, 2022}} On November 18, Smith posted a career–high 18 rebounds to go along with 10 points and 3 blocks in a win over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/381193/jalen-smith-grabs-18-rebounds-friday-night.php|title=Jalen Smith Grabs 18 Rebounds Friday Night|work=FantasyPros.com|date=November 18, 2022}} On November 27, Smith recorded a career–high 23 points on 8–14 shooting along with 9 rebounds in a loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/jalen-smith-career-high|title=Jalen Smith had his most points in a game versus the Clippers on November 27, with 23 points.|work=StatMuse.com|date=November 27, 2022}} Starting in December, Smith would move in and out of the starting lineup, alongside [[Aaron Nesmith]], for the remainder of the [[2022–23 Indiana Pacers season|2022–23 season]]. Smith earned the backup [[Center (basketball)|center]] role behind [[Myles Turner]] for the [[2023–24 Indiana Pacers season|2023–24 season]]. On November 8, 2023, he recorded his first double–double of the season with 16 points, 11 rebounds, 2 steals, and a block, on 5–8 shooting from the field in a win over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-jalen-smith-double-double-off-bench-433971/|title=Pacers' Jalen Smith: Double-double off bench|work=CBSSports.com|date=November 9, 2023}} ===Chicago Bulls (2024–present)=== On July 8, 2024, Smith signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]] on a three-year, $27 million contract.{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Jalen Smith|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-jalen-smith|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2024|access-date=July 8, 2024}} He made 64 appearances (including two starts) for Chicago during the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], averaging 8.2 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 1.0 assist. Smith played in 53 appearances (including 21 starts) for the Bulls in the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], posting averages of 10.2 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 1.2 assists. On March 26, 2026, Smith was ruled out for the remainder of the season due to a right calf injury.{{Cite web|title=Bulls' Jaden Ivey, Jalen Smith out rest of season with injuries|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48313485/bulls-jaden-ivey-jalen-smith-rest-season-injuries|access-date=March 30, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
